title: The “10x engineer:" 50 years ago and now
summary: Gergely Orosz revisits Brooks's surgical team: tooling replaced most roles, hierarchy is dated, and the 10x engineer label can hide context or toxic behaviour.

assertions.quote: the man-month as a unit for measuring the size of a job is a dangerous and deceptive myth

verdicts.note: Brooks's law is supported by communication-overhead models and project data on late staffing.

Lego-team experiment: four-person teams took 53 minutes total versus 36 for two-person teams on the same task and underestimated more (75% vs 55% overrun), and IT projects with more people overrun more often; a workforce twice as large delivers less than twice the output.

assertions.quote: We’ve all seen developers who seem to be a lot more productive than others.
might do so by writing unmaintainable code that several developers will struggle to modify, later
“10x developer” behavior can actually be undetected toxic behavior under a different label

verdicts.note: Plausible confounders; no study separates them from genuine skill differences.

assertions.quote: What didn’t exist back then was source code control and code reviews to stop poorly written code making it to production.

verdicts.note: Review and version control do gate bad code, but flatter teams also reflect cheaper compute; no causal study.
